label: Newborn deaths captured per year
plain_language: The system records about 8,500 newborn deaths a year against roughly 48,000 expected. Most are never counted.
headline: yes

label: Newborn death rate: system vs survey
plain_language: The routine system reports 5.9 deaths per 1,000 births. The national survey found 24, four times higher.
headline: yes

label: Newborn death rate: system vs UN estimate
plain_language: Against the UN's estimate of 21 per 1,000, the routine system still captures only a fraction.

label: Overall monthly reporting completeness
plain_language: Across all 35 hospitals, reports were filed in only 58.3% of the months they were due.
headline: yes

label: Regional hospital reporting (median)
plain_language: Regional referral hospitals filed reports in a median 61.7% of months.

label: Tertiary hospital reporting (median)
plain_language: Tertiary hospitals filed reports in a median of just 50% of months, and none topped 73%.

label: Regional hospitals reporting >75% of months
plain_language: Only 8 of 28 regional hospitals reported in more than three quarters of months.

label: Tertiary hospitals reporting >75% of months
plain_language: No tertiary hospital cleared the 75% reporting bar.

label: Hospitals with consistent year-to-year rates
plain_language: Only 28.6% of hospitals kept their newborn death rate within WHO's consistency band.

label: Share of newborn deaths under-reported
plain_language: More than 75% of newborn deaths go unrecorded in the routine system.

label: Live births that happen in a facility
plain_language: About 80% of Tanzanian births happen in a health facility, so most deaths should show up in facility data.

label: Newborn deaths recorded over 10 years
plain_language: The study covers 34,190 recorded newborn deaths across 35 hospitals over 2015-2024.
